title: West Coast Family Holiday on a Budget: $150‑$250 a Day
meta_desc: Discover how to explore NZ's wild West Coast with a family of four for $150‑$250 daily – free wonders, budget stays, smart savings and splurge tips.
intro: The West Coast may feel remote, but it’s surprisingly affordable for families. With stunning free attractions and a range of budget‑friendly lodgings, you can experience glaciers, pancake rocks and turquoise rivers without breaking the bank.

sections.heading: Budget Basics
sections.body:
For a family of four aim for $150‑$250 each day. Roughly 40% goes to accommodation, 30% to meals, 15% to fuel and transport, and the remaining 15% covers any optional paid activities or souvenirs.

Fuel is the biggest variable – a 2‑hour drive from Greymouth to Franz Josef is about 150km, costing around $30 in petrol for a standard 7‑seat SUV. If you’re renting a car, factor in $70‑$90 per day for a compact SUV, plus insurance.
list: Accommodation: $70‑$110/night
Meals (groceries + occasional eat‑out): $70‑$100/day
Fuel/Car rental: $30‑$45/day
Optional activities: $0‑$40/day

sections.heading: Free & Low‑Cost Adventures
sections.body:
The West Coast’s biggest draw is its natural playground, most of which is free. Arrive early to beat the crowds and capture the best light for photos.

Key free spots include Punakaiki Pancake Rocks (30‑minute walk), the Franz Josef and Fox Glacier terminal‑face walks, and the 25‑minute walk through Hokitika Gorge’s turquoise river path. For a quiet splash, head to Lake Ianthe – perfect for a family swim or a picnic.
list: Punakaiki Pancake Rocks & Blowholes – free, 30‑min walk
Franz Josef Glacier valley walk – free, 3 km return
Fox Glacier viewing platform – free, short walk from car park
Hokitika Gorge walk – free, 1 km trail
Lake Ianthe beach – free, ideal for swimming and picnics

sections.heading: Where to Stay: Cheap to Mid‑Range
sections.body:
Holiday parks and budget motels give you comfort without the price tag. Book early in the shoulder season (April‑May or September‑October) for the best rates.

Options range from basic powered sites for $30‑$45 a night to self‑contained cabins with kitchenettes for $110‑$150. All provide easy access to the main attractions, so you spend less time driving.
list: Punakaiki Beach Holiday Park – powered site $35/night, cabin $95/night
Franz Josef TOP 10 Holiday Park – powered site $40/night, 2‑bed cabin $115/night
Fox Glacier Motel – standard double room $120/night (family of 4)
Hokitika Townhouse Rentals – 2‑bedroom townhouse $130‑$150/night, kitchen included

sections.heading: Food & Transport: Save Smart
sections.body:
Groceries are your best friend. Supermarkets in Greymouth, Hokitika and Franz Josef stock fresh produce, and most holiday parks have shared BBQs for easy family meals.

Plan picnics for the day’s hikes – a sandwich, fruit and a bottle of water costs under $10 per person. If you treat yourselves to a café, aim for $12‑$15 per child and $20‑$25 per adult.
list: Shop at New World (Greymouth) or Four Square (Hokitika) for bulk basics
Cook breakfast and dinner in your accommodation – saves $60‑$80 per day
Use shared BBQs at holiday parks for lunch on the go
Refuel in larger towns where fuel is $1.80/L versus $2.10/L on remote sites

sections.heading: Splurge‑Worthy Experiences
sections.body:
While most highlights are free, a few paid experiences add a memorable wow factor. Choose one or two based on your budget and the kids’ interests.

Guided glacier walks with a certified guide cost $80‑$120 per adult and $40‑$70 per child (5‑12 yrs). A short heli‑flight over Franz Josef is pricey at $250 per person, but you can share the cost with another family to bring it down to $125 each.
list: Guided Franz Josef Glacier walk – $80‑$120 adult, $40‑$70 child
Fox Glacier heli‑flight (30 min) – $250 per person (share to halve)
Kayak tour on the Hokitika River – $90 family package (up to 4)
Greenstone carving workshop in Hokitika – $30 per person

sections.body: Below is a realistic budget for a family of four staying in mid‑range cabins, cooking most meals, and enjoying the free attractions. Adjust accommodation or splurge items to fit your $150‑$250 daily range.
